title: O Holy Night
description: Adolphe Adam's Christmas song of 1847, "Cantique de Noël", in John Sullivan Dwight's English words, for 2 to 4 singers: the first verse and the refrain, "Fall on your knees". The soprano sings the tune; in the refrain the alto, tenor and bass sing the choir parts of a 1916 carol book, and in the verse they sing quiet chords on its organ harmony, moving mostly by step. Slow and lilting, in a gentle 6/8. A stretch song: the tune runs from low C up to E, so take the low notes softly and the high ones gently, or move the key.

credits.words: Placide Cappeau (French, 1847); English words John Sullivan Dwight (1855)
credits.arrangement: Refrain as printed in Carols Old and Carols New (1916); verse set for four voices by Stackapella on its organ harmony

licence.words: public domain: French words 1847, English words 1855 (Dwight died 1893)
licence.arrangement: the refrain's four voices and the verse's organ harmony from Carols Old and Carols New, ed. Charles L. Hutchins (public domain: published 1916, the setting unsigned, Hutchins died 1920), a minor third lower, one note to a syllable: three alto, two tenor and six bass notes changed so the lines move by step; the verse's alto and tenor are Stackapella's, on the organ's harmony, and its bass sings the organ's lowest note, three notes changed and one added where the organ rests; the page's dotted pairs sung in the 12/8 lilt of its triplet accompaniment; breaths written in for beginners
licence.source: Charles L. Hutchins, ed., Carols Old and Carols New, for Use at Christmas and Other Seasons of the Christian Year (Boston: The Parish Choir, 1916), Carol 741, "O holy night. (“Noël.”)", words by J. S. Dwight, Adolph Adam, pp. 617 to 620: the solo line of verse 1, the organ's harmony under it, and the full choir's four-part refrain, in E-flat, written here a minor third lower in C. Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy, archive.org/details/carolsoldcarolsn00huth (leaves 0653 to 0656). The tune checked against Hollis Dann, Christmas Carols and Hymns for School and Choir (New York: American Book Co., 1910), No. 42, "Cantique de Noël", pp. 42 to 46 (archive.org/details/christmascarolsh1910dann), and the refrain's climax against Dudley Buck's arrangement, Christmas Hymn (O Holy Night) (New York: G. Schirmer, 1881), archive.org/details/christmas-anthems-o-holy-night
